mechanics.summary: Move through a detected minefield at one hex per action with no additional movement; make a no-action RECON roll for each entered hex, and failure uses the printed detonation procedure.
exceptions: A line of people needs only its leader to roll; others follow in the leader's footsteps.

unknowns: Mine quantity and detonation procedure are on the preceding printed page.

mechanics.summary: Triggering a blast mine inflicts direct damage to the legs equal to the mine's unmodified damage rating, then triggers an explosion in the hex.

outcome.value: legs direct damage equals unmodified mine damage; then hex explosion

mechanics.summary: Spotting anti-tank mines gives +2 to RECON, canceled by -2 when the RECON roll is made from a vehicle.
trigger: character attempts to spot anti-tank mine

mechanics.summary: Driving unaware into a mined hex automatically triggers an anti-tank mine.
Driving through a detected anti-tank minefield requires one hex per round and a successful DRIVING roll for each hex.
trigger: vehicle drives through detected anti-tank minefield

mechanics.summary: An anti-tank mine inflicts direct damage equal to its unmodified damage rating using the vehicle's rear armor, then triggers an explosion in the hex.

outcome.value: unmodified direct damage using rear armor; then hex explosion

mechanics.summary: Directional mines are individually placed and remotely detonated, usually by tripwire; they cause blast damage only in a front arc typically about 60 degrees, reducing blast one step per three hexes.

unknowns: The printed arc is typical, not fixed.

mechanics.summary: Clearing mines from a hex needs at least one stretch, a TECH roll, and at least a knife or stick; failure detonates a mine.
exceptions: More advanced gear can give positive modifiers, without printed values.

mechanics.summary: Setting up and arming an IED requires explosives, spare parts, one shift, and a successful TECH roll.
exceptions: Failed setup detonates the device immediately.

mechanics.summary: An IED can use tripwire or pressure plate with one general spare part, or electronic remote control or timer with one electronic and one general spare part.
IED shrapnel increases blast power one step to A maximum, requires one additional general spare part, and gives -1 to setting the charge.

A shaped charge gives its directly hit target +1 direct damage, armor modifier 0, and crit rating 1; blast for other targets in the hex is one step lower. Setup is -2 and needs one additional general spare part.
Heavy-weapon direct damage resolves as small-arms fire; its listed blast effect is resolved separately and is not affected by the attack roll.

outcome.value: resolve direct damage and blast separately

mechanics.summary: Hand grenades use MOBILITY instead of HEAVY WEAPONS and have maximum SHORT range.
Pulling a grenade pin is a fast action; grenade throws need no aiming action and suffer no penalty for not aiming.
trigger: actor prepares or throws hand grenade

outcome.value: no aim action or unaimed penalty

mechanics.summary: A grenade landing in the actor's hex permits a no-action MOBILITY roll to drop prone; diving onto it automatically incapacitates the actor, gives a severe torso critical injury using two D10 and the higher result, and protects others in the hex from blast damage.
trigger: hand grenade lands in actor hex

value.dive: incapacitated; severe torso critical injury; 2D10 higher; others avoid blast damage

mechanics.summary: Aiming a heavy weapon is fast except mortars and howitzers are slow; it must be aimed before firing, quick shots are unavailable, and firing is slow.
trigger: actor aims or fires heavy weapon
exceptions: Mortar and howitzer aiming is slow.

mechanics.summary: Heavy weapons receive no bonus for large targets and take -2 when firing at an individual.
Target terrain modifiers apply to heavy weapons except attacks targeting a hex; when targeting a hex, extra attack successes have no effect.

outcome.value: ignore target-terrain modifier and extra-success effect for hex target

mechanics.summary: Heavy-weapons-fire table gives range, individual-target, movement, elevation, terrain, light, weather, and artillery-correction modifiers.

unknowns: Terrain modifier and artillery-correction count require input.

mechanics.summary: Heavy weapons normally use no ammo dice and reload after each shot; reloading is slow with no faster-roll option. A loader or autoloader allows firing every round.
exceptions: Rare printed exceptions can use ammo dice.

mechanics.summary: A failed explosive-effect attack rolls two D6: first direction, second distance in hexes; deviation is capped at half the target distance rounded up.
exceptions: Applies whether target was a hex or specific target.

mechanics.summary: WP rounds have no direct damage; instead of explosion damage they inflict fire damage of intensity equal to blast power, and extinguishing it is -3 to MOBILITY.
CHEM rounds spread nerve or blistering agents over the target area and inflict neither direct damage nor explosive effect.

outcome.value: no direct damage and no explosive effect

mechanics.summary: HEAT rounds have powerful direct damage and an explosive effect.

outcome.value: resolve both direct damage and explosive effect

unknowns: Magnitude is supplied by the printed weapon profile.

mechanics.summary: AP, APDS, and APFSDS rounds typically have direct damage only.

unknowns: The printed qualifier prevents a categorical automatic assumption.

mechanics.summary: ILLUM rounds remove darkness effects within a target-hex radius equal to blast-power die size; at each round beginning roll D6 and a bane ends the flare.
trigger: ILLUM round resolves or new round begins
